title: Methylation and Accumulation in Yeast and Drosophila
summary: This cluster is about the relationship between methylation processes and accumulation of chemicals in yeast and Drosophila. Histone methylation, catalyzed by Dot1, is involved in Arginine methyltransferase. PL methylation produces dimethylphosphatidylethanolamine. Hcy and SAH accumulate in Drosophila and yeast, and are inhibited by Histone methylation, H3K36 methylation, and H3K79 methylation. SAHH causes growth defects in Canton-S and w[1118] and is encoded by Δsah1. Drosophila has PL methylation and accumulates SAH and Hcy. Yeast accumulates Hcy and SAH, has PL methylation, and has proteins ADMA and SAHH.
